q: How do I express use-phase emissions per use, like per wash or per km?
title: Use-phase emissions per wash, km or hour
short: Divide your Category 11 total by the number of uses all products sold that year will deliver over their life. The GHG Protocol's example: 500,000 kg CO2e for 2,000 washing machines at 1,500 washes each is 3,000,000 washes, so 0.1667 kg CO2e per wash.
audience: Makers of fans, pumps, motors, appliances and vehicles reporting Category 11

p: Category 11 counts the whole expected lifetime of every product sold in the year. A fan that lasts longer therefore shows a bigger total, even if it uses less power per hour. The Scope 3 Standard says companies should also report product lifetimes and intensity metrics so durable products are not misread.

sections.h: Pick the unit your buyer compares on
p: Appendix C of the Technical Guidance gives these examples:
ul: Can of cola: kg CO2e per 330 ml can
Washing machine: kg CO2e per wash
Television: kg CO2e per hour of viewing
Car: kg CO2e per km driven

ol: Take the Category 11 total for products sold in the year.
Uses delivered = lifetime uses per product x number sold in the year.
Per-use figure = Category 11 total / uses delivered.

sections.h: Report it beside the total, never instead
ul: The Category 11 total stays the required figure; the per-use number adds context.
Use the same lifetime and use assumptions in both, and publish them.
Other metrics the standard mentions: annual emissions per product, energy efficiency per product, emissions per hour of use, per km or per functional unit.

example.title: Worked example: 4,000 ceiling fans sold in India (assumptions labelled)
lines: Assumed use: 2,500 hours a year for 10 years = 25,000 hours per fan
Per hour of running: 40,50,000 / 10,00,00,000 = 0.0405 kg, about 41 g CO2
A 28 W model on the same assumptions: 0.028 x 0.675 = about 19 g CO2 per hour
example.note: Hours, life and wattage are assumptions for illustration. 0.675 kg CO2 per kWh is the India grid factor for FY 2025-26 (CEA version 22.0); use the grid of the country where the product runs.

senseible: Senseible reads your own bills and purchase invoices; it does not model how customers use the products you sell. Use-phase figures and their assumptions come from you, and can sit beside your Scope 1 and 2 evidence when a buyer asks.
